subject: Cost match play + integration checklist for Datagleam migration
messages:
From: Asha Bhatia <asha@datagleam.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Romero <c.romero@datagleam.com>, procurement@datagleam.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood cost/ops question ahead of exec review

Hi Grace —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Leadership liked the latency profile but procurement pushed back on the headline unit price vs our incumbent. Before our exec sync on Monday they asked for a clear dollars-and-ops comparison:

- A line-by-line vendor price match (token cost, embeddings, LLM-hour reserved pricing)
- One-time migration support credits/engineering hours
- Any non-recurring fees (onboarding, dedicated VPC setup)
- SLA exceptions and rollback/escape clauses

Can you send something that shows where Redwood can match or offset the economic delta — and any operational tasks we should budget for?

Would like to include this in the packet for Monday 10/31.

Best,
Asha
CTO, Datagleam

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Asha Bhatia <asha@datagleam.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood cost/ops question ahead of exec review

Hi Asha —

Appreciate the clear ask. We're pulling together a compact comparator for your packet. High-level play: we can match effective unit economics in two ways — (A) short-term migration credits + dedicated ramp pricing, or (B) modest committed discount with integration support included.

I'm copying Marissa and Jordan to provide the econ sheet and an ops checklist respectively. For the packet I suggest we include:

- One-page cost delta table (current vendor vs Redwood after credits)
- Migration-credit proposal (USD amount tied to go-live within 60 days)
- Integration ops checklist (networking, keys, KV cache warm-up, perf smoke tests)
- A proposed 90-day SLA trial with rollback triggers

Two quick clarifications from your side before we finalize:
1) Do you have a preferred egress/egress-cost bucket for the migration months? (Some customers want us to cover egress during their cutover.)
2) Is Datagleam planning to use Private (VPC) or Dedicated initially? That determines the one-time setup fees.

I’ll route the econ sheet to you by EOD.

Best,
Grace
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Asha Bhatia <asha@datagleam.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood cost/ops question ahead of exec review

Asha / Grace —

Attached is a compact econ sheet (datagleam_econ_sheet.xlsx) and a short note on assumptions. Summary callouts:

- Headline match: We can neutralize the incumbent for year-1 TCO with a $125k migration credit + 20% committed discount on inference units for the first 12 months, subject to a 12-month minimum commitment (commitment level: $450k ARR pre-discount).
- Migration credit mechanics: applied against month-end invoices for the first 3 months; refundable if Datagleam fails to go-live within 60 days (to avoid speculative credits).
- Ops support: 40 engineer-hours included (integration, smoke tests, KV-cache priming). Additional eng hours billed at $250/hr.
- Private vs Dedicated: Private has a one-time infra setup fee of $18k; Dedicated requires a minimum reserved capacity commitment (we proposed an initial 2-GPU pool equivalent).
- Egress: We can absorb egress for the main cutover week up to 10TB. Beyond that we propose a negotiated cap.

I also flagged a small SKU mismatch in their embedding usage vs inference tokens — if they shift embedding loads to batch endpoints we can reduce the effective per-unit cost further.

Attachments: datagleam_econ_sheet.xlsx (tabbed: summary, detailed-calcs, assumptions) and integration_ops_checklist.md (short ops runbook).

Marissa
Head of Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference

From: Carlos Romero <c.romero@datagleam.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@datagleam.com, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood cost/ops question ahead of exec review

Thanks — got the sheet and checklist. A few quick items the execs asked us to confirm before Monday:

1) Can you convert the $125k migration credit into a time-limited onboarding credit that only triggers if go-live happens by 12/31/2026? Execs prefer a hard deadline.
2) We need the ops checklist to call out the on-call rotation during cutover and an expected SLT contact for escalations. Can Jordan or Rishi add a single pager stating who does what?
3) Procurement wants the committed discount expressed as an actual blended $/1M tokens number for comparison (not just %).

If you can send those three clarifications and a signed-statement-of-support (one-pager) we can include in the exec packet. Appreciate the responsiveness.

—Carlos
VP Eng, Datagleam

On Mon, Nov 01, 2026 at 09:02 AM Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks — will get those 3 items over today and add an ops single-pager for on-call/SLT.
